A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GPUDrive with the same authors, simulator design and experimental framework. The complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulator-throughput measurements, reinforcement-learning comparisons and scene-scaling results in Section 4, with goal-reaching, collision and off-road outcomes in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains original simulator and learning experiments, revises the end-to-end training results in Figure 5, and includes the supplementary driving outcomes in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 revises the stated termination procedure: v2 terminates agents upon reaching their goal or colliding, whereas v3 makes collision termination optional. The simulator engine, bicycle dynamics, rewards and IPPO formulation otherwise remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate WOMD driving scenarios, retaining the 10-scenario comparison and larger scene collections. NuPlan and NuScenes appear only as proposed future extensions in v3. New scene illustrations and initialization details do not establish additional evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 3 retains Waymax, original Nocturne and Nocturne parallelized across 16 CPUs; Figure 5 retains Nocturne as the training comparator. PufferLib replaces GPUDrive's training implementation rather than introducing another evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Section 4 changes the implementation used for reported IPPO results from Stable Baselines 3 to PufferLib. Appendix A revises the stated RL hardware from RTX 8000/A100 to RTX 4080/A100. The matched 10-scenario protocol and Table 2 hyperparameters remain unchanged; these disclosures do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The observation-modality speed analysis, scene-count scaling analysis and failure discussion are retained. Appendix D's goal-reaching, vehicle-collision and off-road plots reuse the same images, renumbered from Figure 7 to Figure 8 and enlarged. No new ablation or robustness experiment is reported.

E5.justification: Figure 5 adds shaded uncertainty bands to learning curves and removes the completion-time bar chart with error bars. Both versions report three-seed averages and list seeds 42, 12 and 67 in Table 2. The statistical meaning of the new bands is unspecified.

E6.justification: Section 4.2 revises the reported training speedup over Nocturne from 30–40x to 200–300x and the time to solve 10 scenarios from under 15 minutes to under 3 minutes. Figure 5 is revised, and v3 newly reports 200K–500K controlled agent steps per second for PufferLib PPO. These results concern a changed implementation and reported hardware, not an isolated same-setting simulator improvement.

T1.justification: The ASPS definition, simplified dynamics equation and Appendix B bicycle-model equations and assumptions are unchanged. Numbering the ASPS equation introduces no mathematical revision, and neither version adds theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction expands the released-software contribution from one basic policy-gradient training loop to two training loops. The central claims about million-step throughput, goal-reaching agents and training across thousands of scenarios remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: The conclusion removes specific caveats about training-hyperparameter and reset-overhead bottlenecks, while adding future directions involving multiple datasets and more realistic agents. Section 3.2 replaces the late-appearing-agent explanation with a rationale for filtering trivial goals. The limitations concerning unreachable goals and imperfect driving performance remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds Dockerfile availability, a single-file reproduction workflow taking approximately 16 hours on an A100, and access information for preprocessed WOMD JSON data through Hugging Face. It updates the reproducibility release from v0.2.0 to v0.4.0 and specifies the existing nontrivial-agent initialization threshold as more than two meters from the goal.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Isaac Gym, Panerati et al.'s quadcopter environment, Gigastep and nuScenes. These modestly extend the surrounding literature and future-work context; the positioning against driving simulators and the comparison in Table 1 remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, initialization discussion and concluding future-work passage receive localized rewrites. v3 adds reproducibility, ethics and acknowledgment sections and reorganizes Appendix A. Most of the original exposition and section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds a six-panel simulator-state/agent-view overview, replaces the original scene illustrations, and substantially redesigns Figure 5, including a logarithmic-time learning-curve panel instead of completion-time bars. It relocates the sensor illustration to Appendix A, enlarges Appendix D's plots, updates plotting styles and adopts the conference layout.

improvement.justification: v3 provides clearer reproduction and data-access instructions, specifies agent-selection details, and makes learning variability and simulator observations easier to inspect. These offer a modest overall quality gain. The revised training results use a different implementation, the uncertainty bands remain undefined, and specific training/reset bottleneck caveats disappear without a corresponding diagnostic analysis, limiting the strength of the improvement.
